question: Should universities encourage students to do volunteer work?
transcript: When university students think about learning, classrooms usually come to mind. But can learning also happen outside campus? I believe universities should encourage volunteer work, while keeping participation voluntary. First, volunteering helps students turn knowledge into practical skills because they must explain ideas to people with different backgrounds. For example, last semester I helped younger students with reading at a local community center. At first, I used difficult words, but I soon learned to explain the same idea in a simpler way. This experience made me a more patient communicator. Second, volunteering helps students understand the needs of their community. When we listen carefully to others, we see problems that are easy to miss in a lecture. However, students also need time for coursework and rest, so universities should offer flexible schedules rather than strict requirements. In conclusion, I support volunteer opportunities that connect study with real life. This shows that students can grow while serving others, especially when they have the freedom to choose.
